title: Logical Access Controls

header.html: 3.2 Understand logical access controls: Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP); Separation of Duties (SoD); Access control models
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Subjects, objects and access control

Logical access controls decide who or what (the subject) may do which action on which resource (the object) in computer systems. (Locks and guards are physical controls.)

Term Meaning
Subject The user, process or bot that asks for access
Object The file, database or system being accessed
Access control list (ACL) A list of who may do what on an object
Implicit deny If no rule allows it, the answer is no

2Principle of least privilege (PoLP)

Give each identity only the access it needs to do its job, and no more, for as short a time as needed.

Idea Fact
Need to know Access to information only if the job requires it
Just-in-time access Temporary elevation that expires
Why A stolen or misused account can do less harm; mistakes have a smaller reach
Applies to People, service accounts and AI bots alike
Exam tip

. Least privilege is the default answer when a question asks how to limit damage from a compromised or careless account.

3Separation of duties (SoD)

Split a critical task among two or more people so that no single person can complete it alone. Fraud then needs collusion.

Example Why it helps
The person who creates a vendor is not the person who approves payments One person cannot steal alone
A developer cannot deploy to production; operations does Untested code is less likely

Related ideas: two-person control (two people act together), job rotation, mandatory vacation (fraud shows when someone else covers the job).

Exam tip

. PoLP limits how much; SoD splits who. If a question says no single person should be able to complete the task, the answer is separation of duties.

4Access control models

Model Who decides How
Discretionary (DAC) The owner of the object The owner grants rights to others (flexible, easy to misuse)
Mandatory (MAC) The system, by policy Labels (such as secret) and clearances must match; government and military
Role-based (RBAC) Roles of the job Users get permissions through roles (accountant, nurse)
Attribute-based (ABAC) Rules over attributes Combines user, resource and environment (department, device, time, location)
Rule-based Fixed rules A rule applies to everyone, such as allow only 08:00 to 18:00
Exam tip

. DAC = owner decides. MAC = labels and clearances. RBAC = job role. ABAC = attributes. Rule-based = fixed rules. Do not mix up role-based with rule-based.

5Authentication strength and monitoring

Topic Fact
Factors Something you know, have, are; MFA uses two different kinds
Biometrics Measured by false acceptance rate (FAR), false rejection rate (FRR) and the crossover error rate (CER) where they are equal
Privileged access management (PAM) Extra control and recording of administrator accounts
Behavior analysis Systems, often AI-assisted, spot impossible travel or unusual logins
Exam tip

. A lower CER means a more accurate biometric system. MFA needs different categories, not two passwords.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An analyst needs read access to one report folder for a project that lasts one week. What is the best way to apply least privilege?

  • AGive the analyst administrator rights on the file server
  • BAdd the analyst to the group of all department members
  • CGive read access to that folder only, and remove it after the week
  • DShare the manager's account so access is quick
Show the answer

Answer: C. Least privilege means only the needed access, for the needed time.

S2A company wants the clerk who enters invoices to be different from the manager who approves payment. Which principle is this?

  • ALeast privilege, which limits each account
  • BSeparation of duties, which splits a critical task
  • CDefense in depth, which adds protection layers
  • DNon-repudiation, which prevents denial of actions taken
Show the answer

Answer: B. Splitting a critical task between people is separation of duties.

S3In a system, the owner of a file decides who else can read it. Which access control model is this?

  • ADiscretionary access control based on the owner
  • BMandatory access control based on labels
  • CRole-based access control based on jobs
  • DRule-based access control based on fixed rules for everyone
Show the answer

Answer: A. When the owner decides who gets access, the model is discretionary.

S4Access to a record is allowed only for doctors, from hospital devices, during work hours. Which model uses these attributes of user, device and time?

  • ADiscretionary access control by the owner
  • BMandatory access control
  • CIdentity federation
  • DAttribute-based access control
Show the answer

Answer: D. Attribute-based access control combines attributes of the user, the resource and the environment.

S5A document is labeled secret and only users with a secret clearance can open it, whatever the owner wants. Which model is this?

  • AMandatory access control enforced by the system
  • BDiscretionary access control chosen by the owner
  • CRole-based access control by job title
  • DRule-based access control by time of day
Show the answer

Answer: A. Labels and clearances enforced by the system are mandatory access control.

S6A new accountant is given the permissions that all accountants have through a group. Which model is this?

  • AMandatory access control with labels
  • BDiscretionary access control by the owner
  • CAttribute-based access control with rules
  • DRole-based access control through a role
Show the answer

Answer: D. Permissions assigned through a job role are role-based access control.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does least privilege mean?

Show the answer

Only the access needed to do the job, and no more.

R2What does separation of duties prevent?

Show the answer

One person completing a critical task alone, so fraud needs collusion.

R3Which model lets the owner share access?

Show the answer

Discretionary access control.

R4What is implicit deny?

Show the answer

If no rule allows access, it is refused.

R5What does ABAC use?

Show the answer

Attributes of the user, resource and environment.

R6What does a lower crossover error rate mean?

Show the answer

A more accurate biometric system.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
PoLP minimum access, minimum time; need to know; just in time
SoD split a critical task; collusion needed; job rotation
Models DAC owner, MAC labels, RBAC roles, ABAC attributes, rule-based fixed rules
Biometrics FAR, FRR, CER (lower is better)
Default implicit deny; privileged accounts under PAM
